title: Private Deploy Telemetry and Data Classification Policy
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the telemetry categories, data classification levels, sampling and retention policies, and minimal technical controls required for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for the deployment engineering team, customer security reviewers, and field operations engineers. The goal is to balance operational visibility with customer data protection and cost control.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Private deployments (VPC, dedicated colo racks, air-gapped on-prem installations) delivered and operated by Redwood Inference.
Applies to telemetry produced by: runtime services, control-plane agents, installer/agent tooling, and optional customer integration connectors.
Exclusions: customer application logs and data stored in customer-controlled downstream systems (unless explicitly configured to forward).

Data classification and mapping
-------------------------------
We classify telemetry into four levels. Each level has handling, redaction, and retention requirements.

1) PUBLIC-INFRA
- Example: service health pings, aggregated capacity metrics (node-level CPU%) with no tenant identifiers.
- Handling: no special encryption beyond channel TLS; stored with default retention.
- Retention: 90 days.
- Access: Platform engineers.

2) OPERATIONAL
- Example: per-tenant request rate, queue depths, aggregate latency percentiles (P50/P95) tagged with tenant_id (hashed).
- Handling: tenant_id must be HMAC-hashed using customer-specific salt before leaving tenant boundary; in hosted-managed control planes the tenant is represented by an opaque id. At-rest encryption required (KMS).
- Retention: 180 days.
- Access: SRE, onboarding engineers with RBAC.

3) SENSITIVE
- Example: error traces including truncated stack frames, anonymized request IDs, partial KV cache keys (first 16 bytes only), service-side internal correlation ids.
- Handling: redact any IP addresses and full file paths. Model inputs/outputs that might contain PII are SENSITIVE unless hashed/obfuscated per the telemetry envelope rules below. Must use envelope-level encryption with customer-managed keys when configured.
- Retention: 30 days by default; extendable only by legal/compliance with documented justification.
- Access: Authorized security reviewers and product-onboarding leads.

4) REGULATED / CUSTOMER_PERSONAL_DATA
- Example: raw model inputs/outputs (unredacted), full prompt text, request-level tokens, or any PII/PHI identified by customer or system detectors.
- Handling: shipping of raw inputs/outputs off-box is disallowed by default. If required, customer must opt-in and supply KMS access; data must be pseudonymized or pre-scrubbed. When enabled, data MUST be recorded behind customer-managed envelope encryption and preserved only per a signed data processing addendum (DPA).
- Retention: set by contract; minimum retention is 7 days unless contractually extended.
- Access: strictly controlled (customer representatives, legal, named engineers).

Telemetry categories and required controls
----------------------------------------
A) Metrics\- node and service metrics (Prometheus-style)
- Minimum requirement: Prometheus exposition endpoint bound to local control plane network namespace.
- Export behavior: metrics are aggregated and scrubbed of raw identifiers before being relayed to Redwood telemetry collectors.
- Sampling/rollup: rollup at 1m granularity for cluster-level metrics; tenant-level metrics sampled to 1s/10s depending on configured SLO.

B) Traces
- Minimum requirement: OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing with sampling policy enforced at the agent.
- Default sampling: 0.1 (10%) for high-volume paths; 1.0 (100%) for critical errors and request traces flagged by anomaly detectors.
- Trace scrubbing: remove full request bodies, replace with hashed prefixes and a sparse context map (keys only).

C) Logs
- Minimum requirement: structured JSON logs via local forwarder (file or unix socket) with log-rotation.
- PII detection: built-in regex detectors run at forwarder; any match triggers the log to be sent to an isolated, encrypted bucket and flagged as REGULATED.
- Retention: default 30d for SENSITIVE logs; 7d for REGULATED unless otherwise contracted.

D) Model I/O telemetry
- This is the highest risk category. By default, no raw model inputs or outputs are sent to Redwood.
- Allowed patterns when enabled:
  - Customer opt-in via onboarding manifest (see Onboarding checklist).
  - Data sent only as hashed prefixes + token counts + deterministic quality signals (e.g., repetition_rate, bad_token_ratio).
  - If raw I/O is required for debugging, it must be transported using envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS and stored in a separate, short-lived bucket.

Telemetry envelope and schema (recommended)
-----------------------------------------
All telemetry emitted from tenant-local agents should follow the envelope schema below. Use of this schema ensures consistent redaction and keying. Example envelope (pseudo-JSON, must be applied through agent transform):

{
  \"envelope_version\": \"v1\",
  \"tenant_hash\": \"hmac:sha256:<hex>\",
  \"category\": \"SENSITIVE\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-19T15:04:05Z\",
  \"payload_type\": \"trace/metrics/log/model-io\",
  \"payload_summary\": \"{\\\"tokens\\\":123,\\\"prefix_hash\\\":\"sha256:...\"}\",
  \"signature\": \"sig:<base64>\"
}

Key points: tenant_hash must be generated in-tenant using customer salt; signature is an agent-signed HMAC using the agent keypair. Payloads that include model-io must set payload_type=model-io and be flagged REGULATED unless hashed/obfuscated.

Sampling and cost control policy
-------------------------------
- Default sampling for model-io: 0% (disabled).
- Escalation sampling for debugging: 0.5% global or targeted 100% for a single tenant for up to 72 hours with customer approval.
- Metrics and traces: adapt sampling based on rolling token/signal budget. If a tenant exceeds monthly telemetry quota (defined in onboarding manifest), the control plane will auto-reduce sampling by tiered steps: 100% -> 50% -> 10% -> 1%.
- Storage caps: telemetry retention stores must enforce per-tenant byte quotas. When quota reached, oldest SENSITIVE logs are aged out unless retention is contractually longer.

Onboarding checklist (security & operations)
-------------------------------------------
1) Customer signs DPA if raw model I/O or REGULATED telemetry is required.
2) Customer provides KMS access or accepts Redwood-managed KMS for OPERATIONAL/SENSITIVE (note: REDWOOD-MANAGED KMS allowed only for NON-REGULATED telemetry).
3) Agree on telemetry quota, retention periods, and allowed sampling ceilings.
4) Install tenant agent with agent-keypair and customer salt. Verify tenant_hash generation.
5) Run the telemetry smoke test (CLI below) and capture signed envelope examples.
6) Define escalation contacts and SLOs for telemetry delivery.

Operational runbook and emergency controls
-----------------------------------------
- How to quiesce telemetry for a tenant (operator steps):
  1) Move tenant to telemetry=paused via control-plane API: redwoodctl tenant update --id <tenant> --telemetry=paused
  2) Verify agent acknowledgement: redwoodctl tenant status --id <tenant> | grep telemetry:paused
  3) If network egress remains, apply firewall rule to block agent egress at node level and notify customer.
- How to enable high-fidelity sampling for debugging:
  1) Acquire written customer approval (email or ticket).
  2) Run: redwoodctl tenant update --id <tenant> --telemetry-sample=100 --sample-duration=72h --reason \"debugging incident <INC-#>\"
  3) Monitor storage and revoke after duration.

Audit, evidence and compliance
-----------------------------
Customers and internal auditors must be able to produce:
- Signed telemetry envelope examples and agent public key fingerprint.
- KMS key IDs and access governance logs.
- Sampling policy changes and approval tickets.
- Data flow diagrams showing where model-io is permitted and how it is protected.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Field/onboarding engineer: verify agent key install and tenant_hash behavior.
- Security reviewer (customer-facing): validate DPA and storage controls.
- SRE: configure retention/quotas and monitor telemetry budgets and spikes.
- Product/Legal: approve exceptions and extended retention.

Appendix A: CLI examples
------------------------
Telemetry smoke test (run in customer tenant network):

# publish a sample SENSITIVE envelope locally to verify transform and signature
cat <<EOF > /tmp/example-envelope.json
{
  \"envelope_version\": \"v1\",
  \"tenant_hash\": \"hmac:sha256:abc123...\",
  \"category\": \"SENSITIVE\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-19T15:04:05Z\",
  \"payload_type\": \"trace\",
  \"payload_summary\": \"{\\\"errors\\\":1,\\\"prefix_hash\\\":\\\"sha256:deadbeef\\\"}\",
  \"signature\": \"sig:...\"
}
EOF

# local forwarder check
redwood-agent check --envelope /tmp/example-envelope.json --verify-signature

Enable/disable telemetry via control plane (operator):
redwoodctl tenant update --id t-1234 --telemetry=disabled

Appendix B: Example telemetry retention matrix (plaintext)
-------------------------------------------------------
| Category | Default retention | Max allowed (w/ DPA) | Notes |
| PUBLIC-INFRA | 90d | 365d | Aggregated; no tenant ids |
| OPERATIONAL | 180d | 365d | Hashed tenant ids; KMS at-rest |
| SENSITIVE | 30d | 90d | Requires redaction; limited access |
| REGULATED | 7d | per-contract | Raw model-io only with DPA & CMK |
